h1: The 6 Best Video Switchers Under $300 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Video Switchers Under $300: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 video switchers under $300, from HDMI 2.1 console switches to a streaming mixer, scored on resolution, ports and ease.
summary: The HDMI 2.1 four-input switch is the best pick for a gamer: it lists 8K at 60Hz and 4K at 120Hz for PS5 and Xbox. The acer five-input switch with a remote is the living-room choice, and the FERRISA 4x2 matrix sends sources to two screens at once. For streaming, the rijer live video mixer adds seamless transitions, while the Fosmon RCA box handles old VCR gear.
intro: Most shoppers searching for a video switcher want an HDMI selector, a box that picks one of several inputs for a single TV. A few want a true production switcher with fades and recording. The two groups need different gear, and the biggest mistake is buying a splitter, which copies one source to several screens, when what you need is a switch. The words get mixed up on listings.

We reviewed six switchers, all priced up to the $100 to $200 tier, from their listed ports, resolutions and features. Resolution headroom and port count carried the most weight, then control options like a remote. Listings rarely publish latency or pass-through details, so we ranked what they actually claim.

products.name: HDMI 2.1 Switch 4 in 1 Out 8K 60Hz 4K 120Hz for PS5 Xbox Apple TV
products.verdict: The only HDMI 2.1 switch here, listing 8K at 60Hz and 4K at 120Hz across four inputs.
products.description:
This switch takes up to four HDMI devices into one output and lists 8K at 60Hz and 4K at 120Hz, with HDR and 3D support. It names the PS5, Xbox and Apple TV as targets.

HDMI 2.1 is what matters for current consoles: a 2.0 switch caps at 4K 60Hz, so it quietly drops a PS5 to a lower frame rate. That headroom is why it beats the acer five-input box, which tops out at 4K60.

Buy it if you game on a 120Hz TV. The caveat is that the listing does not mention a remote, and the full chain still has to be HDMI 2.1.

products.name: acer 5 in 1 Out HDMI Switch 4K@60Hz HDMI 2.0 with Remote for PS5 Xbox TV
products.verdict: Five inputs, 4K at 60Hz and a remote for a home theater shelf.
products.description:
The acer expands one HDMI output to five inputs, supports 4K at 60Hz over HDMI 2.0 and 1.4, lists HDCP 2.3 and ships with a remote.

Five inputs cover a TV box, console, Blu-ray player and streamer without unplugging anything, and the remote means you never reach behind a cabinet. It ranks second because HDMI 2.0 caps frame rates below the HDMI 2.1 switch.

Choose it for a media shelf with many sources. The caveat is that 4K120 from a modern console will not pass through it.

products.name: FERRISA 4x2 HDMI Matrix Switch
products.verdict: Four sources to two displays, with any input able to feed either screen.
products.description:
The FERRISA is a 4x2 matrix: four HDMI inputs routed to two outputs. It supports resolutions up to 4K x 2K and LPCM and DTS 5.1 audio.

A matrix does what a basic switch cannot, sending different sources to two TVs at once, which suits a bar or a shared office. It ranks third because 4K x 2K is older and lower than the 4K60 on the acer.

Buy it for two-screen setups. The caveat is the older resolution ceiling and the garbled audio notes in the listing, so check Dolby support if it matters.
products.idealFor: Two-screen setups such as bars and shared offices.

products.name: Live Streaming Video Mixer
products.verdict: An HDMI video mixer with seamless switching and gradual display transitions.
products.description:
This rijer mixer supports common HDMI sources and processes the video signal, with direct seamless switching and gradual display transitions between inputs.

Seamless switching is the difference between a mixer and a selector: a selector blanks the screen for a second while the TV renegotiates, while a mixer cuts cleanly on a live stream. It ranks fourth because it costs a tier or two more, and the listing gives no resolution or input count.

It suits streamers and presenters. The caveat is the missing spec sheet, so confirm inputs and resolution first.
products.idealFor: Streamers who need clean cuts between cameras.
products.skipIf: You just want to swap a console and a box.

products.name: HDMI Switch 4k@60hz Splitter
products.verdict: A three-port HDMI switch at 4K 60Hz for the lowest price.
products.description:
This switch has three HDMI ports, supports 4K at 60Hz and is backward compatible with 2K and 1080p. It is listed as a splitter on the page, which is misleading.

Three ports cover a TV box, a console and a streamer. It ranks fifth because it has fewer ports than the acer's five and no remote is listed.

Buy it for a small TV setup. The caveat is the naming: it switches one of three inputs to one output, and does not split a signal to multiple screens.
products.idealFor: Small TV setups with two or three sources.
products.skipIf: You have four or more sources.

products.name: Fosmon 4-Way RCA Splitter AV Switcher 4 in 1 Out Audio Video Selector Box
products.verdict: A four-input RCA selector for VCRs, DVD players and camcorders, with no power cable.
products.description:
The Fosmon connects up to four RCA AV devices such as VCRs, DVD players and camcorders to one output, needs no separate power cable or drivers, and uses mechanical switch buttons.

It solves a problem no HDMI box can: old analog gear. It ranks last because analog RCA carries standard-definition video, so it is no help for a modern TV.

Buy it to keep legacy equipment alive. The caveat is that the TV needs an RCA input, which many new sets lack.
products.idealFor: Retro gaming and old camcorder tapes.

whatMatters.detail: HDMI 2.0 tops out around 4K at 60Hz, while HDMI 2.1 carries 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz. A modern console on a 120Hz TV needs 2.1 end to end, or the switch quietly lowers the signal. Read the version on the listing, and match it to your cables and display.

A switch chooses one of several inputs for one screen. A splitter copies one input to several screens. Listings blur the words, so the product title can mislead. Read the port description, such as 3 in 1 out, to confirm you are buying the direction you need.

Count every source you own, then add one for growth. Four sources fit a four-port switch, but a console, streamer, Blu-ray and cable box already fills one. Remember each device uses an input, so a five-input box like the acer spares you from swapping cables later.

A basic selector blanks the screen for a second or two while the display re-handshakes. A mixer cuts instantly and can fade between sources, which matters on a live stream. Look for the words seamless switching or transitions on the listing if the output goes to viewers.

Buttons on the box are fine if it sits within reach, but a shelf behind a cabinet needs a remote. Check the listing for a remote, as the acer lists, or mechanical buttons, as on the Fosmon, and decide where the unit will live before buying.

faq.q: Will the acer work with a PS5?
faq.a: Yes, at up to 4K and 60Hz over HDMI 2.0. It is named for PS5 and Xbox use, but 4K at 120Hz needs the HDMI 2.1 switch, which lists that frame rate explicitly.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with video switchers?
faq.a: Confusing a switch with a splitter. The HDMI Switch 4k@60hz Splitter is actually a three-input switch. If you want one source on two TVs, a splitter or the FERRISA 4x2 matrix is the right tool.

faq.q: Is the rijer mixer worth it over the acer?
faq.a: Only for streaming. The rijer cuts seamlessly and fades, but costs more and lists no inputs. The acer offers five clear HDMI inputs and a remote, which suits a TV far better.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Plug each source into an input, run one cable from the output to the TV, and select the active input with the button or remote. The Fosmon works the same way for RCA gear and needs no power.

faq.q: Does the Fosmon work with modern TVs?
faq.a: Only if the TV still has RCA or composite inputs. Otherwise add a converter. It is meant for VCRs, DVD players and camcorders, and carries standard-definition video, not HD.

faq.q: Can the FERRISA send two different sources?
faq.a: Yes. As a 4x2 matrix it routes any of its four HDMI inputs to either of two outputs, so two TVs can show different sources. A plain selector like the acer shows one.

finalTake: The HDMI 2.1 four-input switch is the pick for gamers because it alone lists 4K at 120Hz. The acer five-input box is the sensible living-room choice with its remote. The FERRISA matrix is the answer for two screens, and the rijer mixer only makes sense for live streaming. Always check whether a listing sells a switch or a splitter.
